raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

OpenAI's `reasoning_effort` accepts none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. DeepSeek-V4.1's encoder names low (50), high (75) and max (100) on a 1-100 budget, with xhigh as an alias of high (#39929). So `minimal` and `medium` fell back to the default `high` with a server-side warning, and `minimal` got more reasoning than `low`.

## Modifications

- `parse_dsv41_reasoning_effort` maps `minimal` to 50, the same as `low` (Harmony also maps minimal to low), and `medium` to 62, between `low` and `high`.
- The same applies to `SGLANG_DSV41_REASONING_EFFORT`.
- The encoder is unchanged.
- Rust `sglang-processor` render matches.
- The cookbook, the environment variable reference and the warning text list the new levels.

## Accuracy Tests

Only `minimal` and `medium` render differently, as budget 50 and 62 instead of 75.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Validation

- **Python:** a new test in `test_serving_chat.py` covers the parsed values, the environment default and the rendered prompt through `_process_messages`. It fails before the change and passes after.
- **Rust:**
  - The render parity fixture gains `effort_minimal`, and `effort_medium` now expects budget 62. The fixture was generated with the V4.1 tokenizer.
  - The parity test fails with the old code.
  - A unit test covers the budget mapping.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
